---
title: "Case-report specification and export"
subtitle: "T.2 · after the postrank theory book, chapter 21, and the reading/exporting vignette"
description: "Reports accompanied by target definitions, computation scope, error-budget checks and source information."
---

Reports are calculated from released probabilities under declared targets, losses and families.
Error-budget rows evaluate the displayed report without selecting a constrained alternative. The reporting view
retains assumptions, computation scope and conditioning, with drafting and download controls.
Browser results are distinguished from archived statuses and bounds.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/report-designer.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["report-designer"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **CDE: three-grade family.** The browser enumerates all 523,251 capped reports. The chosen report states
  45 pairs. The family label, criterion profile and fixed-archive comparison define the reported computation scope.
  These twelve schools are a deliberately spread teaching subset, not a representative statewide sample.
- **KRW: equal weights.** The report states 636 pairs and is optimal within this order: the weighted expected-rank
  order. The order and its report family are recomputed when the error weight changes. The supplied marginal intervals describe
  individual targets; no joint race–gender posterior or Gaussian replacement is created.
- **Alabama: equal weights.** The report states 1,249 pairs. Grade 1 means favourable historical outcomes,
  including lower incarceration, rather than greatest need. Source conditioning and the supplied interval level
  stay attached to the case and its model TXT.
- **CDE: cap two.** The family contains 4,095 reports. Its risk and the archived risk use the same withholding cost. Changing a cap changes the family; it does not make same-loss evaluations incomparable.
- **CDE: mean-order cap four.** The computation switches to the posterior-mean order. It is optimal only among
  cuts of that order. The budget rows still evaluate the displayed report and show signed count-form slack.
- **CDE: all withheld.** E/N reads NA: no disclosure. A homogeneous budget passes without stating anything,
  so passing alone is not evidence of informative or error-free reporting. The reporting view retains these qualifications in the download.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Current and archived settings appear together; the old status, bound and gap never certify a new browser DP. Shared grades
withhold directions, not assert equality; expected error shares do not give joint correctness. Allocation needs
another decision rule. Draft text remains in component memory, outside the URL, iframe state and storage.

CDE's prior conditions on the statewide fit. KRW uses historical contact-gap targets from
[Kline, Rose and Walters](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20230700) and their
[data deposit](https://doi.org/10.3886/E198284V1), under the deposit’s CC-BY-NC terms (no version stated); this extraction does not describe current conduct.
Alabama uses [Opportunity Atlas](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/NKCQM1) historical outcomes under CC BY 4.0.
Each case retains its complete attribution, changes and conditioning below the app and in downloads.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The mean-order cap-four result states 54 pairs, with risk .0368858. With postrank 1.1.0 loaded:

```r
x <- pr_case_cde$input; s <- postrank_settings(weights = c(negative_chronic_absence = 1), tau = .2, G_max = 4)
a <- postrank_cuts(x$summaries$means[, 1], x, s, direction = "descending", rule = "optimal")
a$evaluation[c("N", "E_over_N", "primary_risk")]
```
:::
